fact_check_log.claim: Takeaway 4: lab-grown and natural diamonds look and behave essentially the same; get natural or lab-grown confirmed in writing on receipt and report.
Fluorescence does not cause haziness on its own; it can only intensify haziness already present in rare stones.
GIA study of E, G, I and K stones: no systematic effect for average observers; strongly blue stones seen as better colour table up.
In practice, fluorescence rarely changes how a stone looks (summary of the GIA study and rarity of haziness).
Blue fluorescence can make an I to M stone look more colourless in daylight without changing the grade; view in person under different lighting and compare same-grade stones.
FAQ: fluorescence intensifies haziness only in rare stones that already have it; view in daylight beside same-grade stones.
ABF: AUD900 general goods allowance for travellers 18 and over, jewellery counts, as at October 2026 (travel section and FAQ only).
Wedded Concierge plans venue, travel, vendors and payments anywhere in the world, with one Wedded Advisor as single point of contact.
The fee is agreed in writing before any work begins; the Wedded Advisor confirms inclusions in writing before you commit.
Your Wedded Advisor confirms the current requirements for carrying and declaring a ring before you travel (compliance-checklist wording, framed for Concierge couples).
We found no independent published comparison of GIA and IGI that we could cite.
Australian Consumer Law prohibits misleading or deceptive conduct.
